findings.title: Diff-truncation accounting fits the existing `_inject_file_contents` shape
findings.description: The decision to make `_inject_file_contents` return `(prompt, DiffInjection)` and reuse `_add_injection`'s existing return value (D3) is grounded in verified source (`src/squadron/review/review_client.py:373, 416, 424`). The two call sites listed in Implementation Notes (`test_content_injection.py`, `test_convention_root.py`, `test_injection_decision.py`, `test_review_client.py`) are reasonable to expect for a helper with two existing callers. The byte-identical `clean_pass_artifact.md` invariant is correctly anchored on a hand-built result with no diff (`tests/review/test_persistence.py:879`), so Part A cannot regress the snapshot fixture.

findings.title: Part B cap logic is correctly bounded and sequenced
findings.description: The rule (truncated AND no successful tool call AND PASS → CONCERNS + synthetic finding + `verdictSource: imposed`) uses the verified `tool_calls_made` and `failed_tool_calls` fields from `ReviewResult` (`src/squadron/review/models.py:134, 158`). The decision to place `impose_diff_coverage` in its own module (`review/coverage.py`) is correctly motivated by the noted 588-line size of `review_client.py` and the slice plan's explicit "is not this slice's job" framing for refactoring injection into its own module. The ordering call ("must run after `tool_calls_made`/`failed_tool_calls` are assigned, and after the #92 recovery turn") is correct: those are the only two events that mutate the telemetry fields between parsing and persistence, and the existing `_stamp_tool_telemetry` callers in both providers set the fields on the final `Message` before yielding.

findings.title: Part C model-identity capture is correctly grounded in SDK and OpenAI provider surfaces
findings.description: The SDK claim that `AssistantMessage.model` and `parent_tool_use_id` exist on the pinned 0.2.152 is consistent with the 920 design's verified compatibility surface. The OpenAI claim that `chunk.model` is on every `ChatCompletionChunk` (including choice-less usage chunks) matches the SDK's typed delta shape. The decision to stamp `metadata["answering_models"]` as a new key rather than repurposing the existing OpenAI `metadata["model"]` (which holds the requested id) preserves a useful distinction. The Codex-as-not-reported handling in D11 — keeping the requested id and surfacing it in the Run Digest rather than fabricating `unknown` or collapsing all Codex judges into one metrology identity — correctly applies the project's "no silent fallback values" principle.

findings.title: D9 snapshot-equivalence rule is appropriately conservative
findings.description: The rule (`gpt-5` → `gpt-5-2025-08-07` is not a substitution; `gpt-5` → `gpt-5-mini` is) is narrow by design and the rationale is documented: a false substitution costs one extra frontmatter key, a missed substitution is the bug this slice exists to fix. The plan to capture each profile's real ids in Phase 6 walkthrough step 6 before adding forms to the rule, with tests built from captured ids, is exactly the right calibration sequence — it matches the project's "test fixture must include the actual format that parser will consume in production" rule.

findings.title: Scope cuts are correctly identified and deferred
findings.description: The exclusions (`max_file_size_bytes` defaults, #114, #137 diff ordering and `--stat`, #138 file-body truncation, `judge-findings-addressed`'s `round_diff`, provider-failure artifacts in D13) each have a stated reason, and each maps to a separate slice or issue. D13's reasoning — that provider-failure artifacts have no `ReviewResult` and therefore no answering model to record — is correct against `format_provider_failure_markdown` (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:553+`), which builds the frontmatter from raw values rather than from a result.

findings.title: Integration parity with both execution paths is structurally enforced
findings.description: The data-flow diagram correctly shows both `sq review` and `pipeline/actions/review.py` calling `run_review_with_profile` then `save_review_result` → `format_review_markdown`. Verified: `format_review_markdown` is the single rendering function used by both paths (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py`), so every fact on `ReviewResult` reaches both the CLI terminal header (via the same Markdown body that includes `**Model:**` and `**Diff:**` lines) and the pipeline `ActionResult.metadata` (via the explicit `metadata["model"]` assignment). The `pipeline/actions/review.py` change to also set `metadata["requested_model"]` is the minimal closure.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough probes both new failure shapes
findings.description: Steps 1–5 force the truncation paths and the untruncated path on the slice's own diff (which is a real test subject, not a fixture); step 6 captures per-profile real answering ids to feed D9. The two acknowledged live-test limitations — Part B's behavior under `-v` is observed rather than asserted, and a real substitution cannot be forced against live providers — are honestly recorded, and SC9 (stubbed provider with mismatched id) covers the substitution case in unit tests.

findings.title: Failure-mode coverage for new I/O paths
findings.description: Part A reads from in-process state (no new I/O). Part B's `impose_diff_coverage` is a pure function over `ReviewResult` fields (no I/O). Part C's two provider paths read model id off already-streamed chunks/messages (no new I/O). None of the three parts introduce a new external call, message type, or subprocess that would need hang/timeout/peer-disconnect enumeration. The persistence and rendering paths are local file I/O already covered by the existing archive-and-overwrite guard.

structured_findings.summary: Diff-truncation accounting fits the existing `_inject_file_contents` shape
Part B cap logic is correctly bounded and sequenced
Part C model-identity capture is correctly grounded in SDK and OpenAI provider surfaces
D9 snapshot-equivalence rule is appropriately conservative
Scope cuts are correctly identified and deferred
Integration parity with both execution paths is structurally enforced
Verification walkthrough probes both new failure shapes
Failure-mode coverage for new I/O paths
